refusals.sshHostMissing: Give the address of the SSH server.
refusals.hostMissing: Give the address of the database.
refusals.notAHost: Enter a hostname or an IP address, without the rest of a URL.
refusals.pickTunnel: Pick the server to tunnel through.
refusals.pickJump: Pick the server to jump through.
refusals.connectionGone: That connection is not there any more.
refusals.passphraseAlone: Paste the private key this passphrase is for, or clear the passphrase.
refusals.tunnelNotYours: The server to tunnel through is not one of yours.
refusals.jumpNotYours: The server to jump through is not one of yours.
refusals.sshPassword: Enter the password for the SSH login.
refusals.sshKey: Paste the private key for the SSH login.
refusals.notYours: That database is not one you can open.
refusals.tunnelGone: The server this connection tunnels through is not one of yours any more.
refusals.sshIncomplete: This connection's SSH login is incomplete. Edit it and save it again.
refusals.jumpGone: The server this tunnel jumps through is not one of yours any more.
refusals.databaseGone: That database is not there any more.
refusals.objectStore: An object store is browsed from its Buckets panel, not as a database.
refusals.unpublished: This database runs on another server and is not published on a port, so Polaris cannot reach it from here. Publish it on a port from the database's own screen, then open it again.
refusals.unpublishedShort: Runs on another server and is not published on a port, so Polaris cannot reach it from here.
refusals.redisCluster: A Redis cluster spreads its keys over several masters, and the browser reads one server at a time, so it cannot open one.
refusals.noSuchName: There is nothing here by that name.
refusals.notEditable: Values in this kind of database are not edited from the grid.
refusals.redisOnly: Only a Redis key has a value to open.
refusals.noPrimaryKey: This table has no primary key, so there is no way to change one row of it without risking the others. Use the statement box.
refusals.primaryKeyColumn: That column is part of the primary key. Changing it moves the row, so it goes through the statement box.
refusals.rowUnknown: That row cannot be identified - the page it came from did not carry its whole primary key.
refusals.mongoEmpty: Type a command document, for example '{' find: "users", limit: 20 '}'.
refusals.mongoNotJson: That is not a command document. Mongo takes JSON here, for example '{' find: "users", filter: '{' active: true '}', limit: 20 '}' - with the field names quoted.
refusals.noColumns: That table has no columns to read.
refusals.noOrderColumn: No such column to order by.
refusals.keyGone: That key is not there any more.
refusals.generic: That did not work. Nothing was changed.
refusals.readOnly: This connection is read-only, and {what} would change the database. Turn read-only off on the connection if you meant to.
refusals.sshSignInJump: Polaris could not sign in to {target} over SSH through {jump}. Check the address, the user and the {secret}.
refusals.sshSignIn: Polaris could not sign in to {target} over SSH. Check the address, the user and the {secret}.
refusals.loginUnreadable: Polaris cannot read the login stored for {server}. Add that server again under Servers, then save this connection.
refusals.noHostKey: Polaris has no key on record to check {server} against, so it will not tunnel through it. Remove it under Servers and add it again, then save this connection.
refusals.tunnelFailed: Polaris could not open the SSH tunnel through {server}. Check that the server is up and that the login still works.
refusals.keyChanged: {target} answered with a different key than the one Polaris pinned for this connection, so nothing was sent to it. If that server was rebuilt, remove this connection and add it again.
